overall_summary: Data reveals that 'self respect' digital boundaries (blocking, deleting chats, status updates) combined with family emotional bonds (Maa, Papa) massively outperform romantic heartbreak loops. Family bonds (Maa/Papa videos) generated the highest views (up to 215) and engagement (likes), while romantic/self-respect status updates performed moderately well (up to 41 views), and extremely granular digital actions (changing ringtones, removing profile from streaming accounts) suffered from low engagement/fatigue.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos about parents (Maa, Papa) secured the highest overall views (215 and 122) and likes (18 and 11) compared to romantic heartbreak or niche digital actions.
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate parental care and sacrifice into emotional storytelling to expand reach beyond niche relationship content.

winning_patterns.evidence: Mid-tier success (30-41 views) was found in clear, universally understood self-respect actions regarding status lists and read receipts (e.g., 'स्टेटस लिस्ट में सबसे ऊपर उन्हीं का नाम था').
winning_patterns.action: Focus self-respect narratives on universally relatable phone behaviors rather than hyper-niche app actions.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on very specific UI elements like streaming account profiles, ringtone defaults, or shared albums got almost zero traction (0-3 views).
weak_patterns.action: Avoid overly specific or obscure digital breakup triggers that alienate casual viewers.
